requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: the three migrations match the data model, including a composite PK on totem_preset_queue (database/migrations/..._create_totem_preset_queue_table.php:24). totem:pairing-code uses random_int with zero-padding, a 10-minute expiry, clears consumed_at, audits and returns FAILURE for an unknown id (app/Actions/OpenTotemPairingWindow.php:22-34, app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:20-27). Auth returns 400 for a bad format, including non-strings and empty input (TotemAuthController.php:17). Unknown, expired, consumed and inactive codes all give the same 401. Pairing runs in a transaction with lockForUpdate and returns the entity pair (PairTotem.php:28-31, 177-183). The JWT has all the required claims (PairTotem.php:160-168). The middleware covers every 401 case and intersects the claimed queues with the preset's current join (AuthenticateTotem.php:682-711). Endpoints return 403 forbidden for the wrong entity, 404 when the queue is not found inside the entity, and 403 when the queue is out of scope. Inactive queues give 422 and invalid priorities give 422. Issuance goes through IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TotemTicketController.php:622). Throttles are 10/min and 30/min, and api/* renders 429 rate_limited (routes/api.php:9,17; bootstrap/app.php:1143-1149). CORS allows localhost and 127.0.0.1 on any port plus TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN, and preflight answers 204. config, .env.example and phpunit.xml are updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are new Actions (PairTotem, OpenTotemPairingWindow) and issuance reuses IssueTicket. Models use #[Fillable] deliberately. Migration filenames are timestamped like generator output and each has a reversible down(). CHANGELOG, docs/api/totem.md, architecture.md, database-schema.md and business-rules.md are all updated. Deviations: input is checked by hand instead of $request->validate (TotemAuthController.php:449, TotemTicketController.php:614-619), although the custom error codes justify it. docs/api/totem.md:1613 says description is null, but TotemQueueController.php:563 reads labels_i18n['description'].

security.evidence: HS256 accepts only alg=HS256, compares with hash_equals, enforces exp, and throws if the secret is missing (TotemJwt.php:1028-1042, 1052). Codes are never logged, and failures give the same 401 so there is no oracle. Pairing is single-use under a row lock. Queues are resolved inside the token's entity only (TotemApiController.php:405-408). Scope is checked again against the live join on every call. CORS does not use a wildcard or allow credentials. Minor gap: the >=32-char secret length is not enforced at runtime, so a short TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is accepted silently (TotemJwt.php:1052).

tests.evidence: Nine feature test files cover: schema, factory and relations; the command (window, replacement, unknown id, audit); auth (every format case, unknown, expired, consumed, inactive, success claims, double use, 429, audit without the code); middleware (missing, malformed, bad signature, expired, inactive totem or preset, entity mismatches, deleted totem, last_seen_at, live scope shrink); queues ordering and position; priorities exact JSON, inactive, cross-entity 404, out-of-scope 403; tickets (201, sequential codes, invalid priority datasets with no rows created, inactive, scope, wrong entity, 429); and CORS allowed and denied origins. One small flaw: the 'missing key' dataset row duplicates 'null' (TotemAuthTest.php:1985-1986).

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses IssueTicket and keeps TicketPriority as the single source for the endpoint and for validation. The hand-rolled JWT is about 120 lines, which the task allows. There is some extra indirection: a TotemApiController base class, a TotemContext value object and a QueueVisual crc32 colour palette (app/Support/QueueVisual.php). The inactive-queue check is duplicated in the controller and in the IssueTicket catch (TotemTicketController.php:610-625), and ->values() after get() is redundant (TotemQueueController.php:552).

readability.evidence: Classes are small and focused, names are clear, and PHPDoc array shapes are provided (TicketPriority.php, PairTotem.php:107). Comments explain non-obvious choices, such as the global CORS prepend (bootstrap/app.php:1134-1135). Style is consistent and there is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. One unrequested change: phpunit.xml now pins APP_KEY (phpunit.xml:1918), which the task did not ask for. The docs/README.md and business-rules.md edits are reasonable doc syncing.

issues.explanation: The doc says queue `description` is always null, but TotemQueueController.php:563 returns labels_i18n['description'] when it is set (the test at TotemQueuesTest.php:2558 asserts that), so the doc and the code disagree.
Pins an APP_KEY in phpunit.xml, which is unrelated to the totem secret and TTL the task asked to pin.
Only checks that the secret is non-empty, so a weak or short TOTEM_JWT_SECRET in production is accepted without any warning.
Input is validated by hand instead of with the project's $request->validate pattern; this is defensible for custom error codes, but it is not explained.
The 'missing key' dataset row passes ['code' => null], the same as the 'null' row, so the case where the key is truly absent is not tested.
->values() after ->get() is redundant, because the collection is already zero-indexed.

review.summary: Implements the totem BFF: three tables with models and factories, a pairing command, atomic single-use pairing with an HS256 JWT, a totem.auth middleware with a live queue-scope intersection, the three endpoints (issuance reuses IssueTicket), JSON throttling, and local-origin CORS. Docs and tests are thorough. The requirements, security and tests are all strong. Only minor issues remain: one doc/code inconsistency about queue descriptions, an unrequested APP_KEY in phpunit.xml, and no runtime check of the secret's strength. I would approve with nits.
